newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ curve ends flatter as bills rally, bonds weaken.
newsitem.headline: NZ curve ends flatter as bills rally, bonds weaken.

* NZ yield curve flattens as bills rally, bonds soften
* Firmer TWI perks up money market
* Bond tender successful but focus still on offshore mkts
New Zealand's yield curve flattened on Thursday as bond rates rose a touch from their morning levels but short rates rallied on the back of a stronger currency.

Dealers said today's tender of NZ$100 million February 2001 government bonds had been relatively successful, with an average yield of 7.185 percent, but bonds weakened slightly as the market focused on the performance of offshore markets.
"Bonds are apathetic on the back of the fact that no other dollar bloc really has rallied strongly," said a dealer.

"Australia is weakening, I think people are watching that. The U.S. isn't particularly strong, and given the fact that the last (economic) figures we've had were quite weak....our inflation outlook isn't clearcut."
The short end, on the other hand, rallied about seven points to recoup yesterday's losses.
"It's been a far more positive day. I think the dollar's been squeezed a little bit, it's up again and that's the primary reason why we have rallied," a dealer said.
The Kiwi's Trade-Weighted Index rose nearly 30 points from Wednesday's close, but dealers were still apprehensive that the currency would again be sold in the United States overnight.
One also noted that the money market, despite today's rally, was long. "It is a very long market. People are still selling," the dealer said, adding that volumes were light.
